subject: Renewal design: multi-year float + burst credits (proposal)
messages:
From: Nora Patel <nora.patel@zenfolio.io>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Morris <evan.morris@zenfolio.io>
Date: 2026-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal conversation kickoff

Dylan —

We’re starting to plan Zenfolio’s renewal for Oct 1. Headline ask from finance: avoid a hard annual prepay, but give us predictable unit economics and the ability to burst in Q4 for the holiday launch. Can you propose a structure that: (1) spreads commitment across 24 months but doesn’t require full prepay, (2) includes a mechanism for short-term bursts, and (3) keeps pricing simple for our procurement?

Nora
Director of Platform Engineering
Zenfolio

Attachment: usage_forecast_q3q4.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@zenfolio.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-03T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation kickoff

Nora — thanks for the clear asks. High level idea below; I’ll follow with a one‑page amendment and sample numbers.

Proposal summary (conceptual):
- 24‑month floating commitment: Zenfolio commits to an annualized token volume, invoiced quarterly (no up‑front full-year prepay). Quarterly invoicing smooths cash flow.
- Stair‑step ramp: first 3 quarters at 60% of baseline, then 85% / 100% to reach steady state—this protects you during onboarding windows.
- Burst overlay: a separate burst credit bucket you can consume at a higher short‑term rate but with guaranteed availability during specified windows (e.g., Nov 15–Dec 31).
- Co‑term: allow existing smaller line items to be co‑termed into the 24‑month contract to simplify renewal cadence.
- Simple pricing ladder: baseline unit price, burst unit price (x1.6), and multi‑year discount if renewal triggers prior to 12 months.

Next steps: I’ll draft an amendment (no legalese) and run numbers with finance and Marissa to confirm SLA/credits. Can you confirm if Zenfolio needs a KMS/HSM clause for Private deployment options?

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: zenfolio_draft_amendment_v1.pdf (draft)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-05T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal conversation kickoff

Team — forwarding Nora’s ask and Dylan’s sketch. Quick internal notes before we finalize numbers: 

1) Finance prefers quarterly invoicing vs monthly for committed portion (reduces billing churn).
2) Recommend we include a convertibility clause: unused baseline in Q1–Q2 can be shifted into burst credit at a discounted conversion for the customer to avoid perceived waste.
3) Legal will push on termination for convenience on multi‑year; suggest we offer a 90‑day early‑exit pro rata with a small fee.
4) Marissa: can you prepare two P&L scenarios (conservative/adoptive) with expected ARR movement and show unit economics impact for Redwood?

—Marissa
VP, Renewals & Growth

Evan/Nora — appreciate the redlines. Quick answers and next steps: 

1) SLA for burst windows: we can commit to a 99.5% availability for reserved burst capacity during defined windows. If we fail to meet the SLA, customer receives credit against the burst bucket at 1.5x the affected units.
2) Conversion of unused baseline: we’ll add a one‑time conversion right for Q1–Q2 per Marissa’s suggestion (conversion price = 0.9x baseline unit).
3) Early exit: propose a 90‑day notice with pro rata refund less a 5% administrative fee.
4) DocuSign + quarterly invoice path: I’ll generate the DocuSign envelope and HubSpot will be updated with the DocuSign link; finance will set quarterly invoice terms on the deal record.

I’ve attached the clean amendment with the SLA and conversion language; legal redlines are in the doc you sent — we’ll align and produce final v2 by Monday.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Renewals Lead, Redwood Inference
